Prices turn tokens into charges.

A token is a unit of model input or generated output. Input includes the instructions, context and image tokens. Output includes billable reasoning tokens when the selected mode produces them.

Table 1. Report price snapshot · USD per million tokens
ModelInputOutput
Qwen3.8-Max$2.00$6.00
Qwen3-VL-Plus$0.20$1.60

Historical rates reproduced from report Table 4; vision input tier ≤ 32,000 tokens. T = Qwen3.8-Max, V = Qwen3-VL-Plus throughout the call table.

Charge (USD) = (input tokens × input price + output tokens × output price) / 1,000,000

Response time needs a defined scope.

The records distinguish one observed response, a configured deadline, and the workflow statistics that still need measurement. p95 means 95% of measured requests finish within that time.

Table 5. Timing evidence and its scope
ItemTime / statisticEvidence typeWhat the record covers
Text API connectivity sampleAbout 3.4 sObserved sampleOne successful solar-energy text request, HTTP 200; live integration note dated 2026-10-04. This request differs from the navigation workflows.
Model request timeout60 s / callConfigurationThe provider aborts an individual model request after 60,000 ms. This limit describes a request deadline.
Navigation workflow latencyMedian / p95 pendingMeasurement pendingThe saved integration note records successful workflow outcomes without a latency distribution. Photo workflows contain two sequential model calls plus local processing.
Text workflow1 model call + local validation
Photo workflowVision → local retrieval → text matching → local ranking

The 3.4-second sample provides connectivity evidence. It does not supply navigation-workflow averages. Measure each complete workflow from request submission to usable result; record sample count, median, p95 and failures together.

Quality has explicit acceptance targets.
